title: Split ArticleDrawer into state hook + view
description:
# Brief 1: split ArticleDrawer into state hook + view (no visible change)

## Why
A later change adds an inline reading pane next to the article list. It must show
the same article UI as the slide-out drawer. This step only separates logic from
presentation so both can share it. Nothing may change for the user.

## Repo
/Users/m/git/refusion, frontend in `frontend/`. Read `AGENTS.md` (root) first.

## Files allowed
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-drawer.tsx` (edit)
- `frontend/src/components/article/article-view.tsx` (new)
Touch nothing else. No git commands.

## What to do
1. In `article-view.tsx`, export a hook `useArticleViewState()` that contains,
   moved unchanged, everything `ArticleDrawer` computes today before its `return`:
   URL state, `useArticleList`, mutations, read-state pins, the article/readArticle
   resolution, `useAutoMarkRead`, all handlers, and `useArticleNavigation`.
   Keep every existing comment, word for word, next to the code it explains.
   It returns what the JSX needs (article, readArticle, canToggleRead, feed,
   bookmark, starred, safeArticleLink, the handlers, goToNext/goToPrevious/
   hasNext/hasPrevious, and a `close()` that calls `setSelectedArticle(null)`).
2. In the same file, export `ArticleView({ state, variant })` with
   `variant: "drawer" | "pane"`. It renders the header, content and footer
   exactly as the drawer's JSX does today, and returns `null` when there is
   no article. `SheetTitle` (sr-only) renders only for `variant === "drawer"`.
   `getLinkDomain` becomes a module-level function in this file.
3. `ArticleDrawer` becomes a thin shell: it calls `useArticleViewState()` at its
   top level (outside the Sheet), then renders the same `<Sheet>`/`<SheetContent>`
   as today with `<ArticleView state={state} variant="drawer" />` inside.

## Hard constraints (these are the bugs to avoid)
- The hook must run in `ArticleDrawer` itself, never inside `SheetContent`.
  Today the logic runs while the drawer is closed; `useAutoMarkRead` relies on
  seeing its target go to `null` when the article closes. Moving the hook inside
  the Sheet would unmount it on close instead and change that behaviour.
- `useArticleNavigation` must still be called exactly once by the drawer path,
  with the same `enabled: selectedArticleId !== null` and the same callbacks.
  A second call registers a second keydown handler and `j` skips articles.
- No renames of i18n keys, CSS classes or props; no new dependencies;
  no behaviour or styling changes; no "while I'm here" cleanups.
- Comments only where the repo's rules say so (`AGENTS.md`, Code Standards).

## Checks (run in `frontend/`, all must pass)
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm run check:i18n`

## Report back
- The checks' last lines.
- Any place you could not move code unchanged, and why.
acceptance_criteria: In frontend/: pnpm run typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm run check:i18n pass; diff -w of old drawer vs article-view.tsx shows only the hook/view seams; drawer click-through unchanged.

title: 3-pane reading layout (opt-in)
description: Opt-in panes layout as an alternative to the article drawer. Spec and decisions in design.
design:
Spec: opt-in 3-pane reading layout (feeds | article list | article) next to the existing slide-out drawer.
Plan: (1) split ArticleDrawer into useArticleViewState() + ArticleView, no visible change; (2) readingLayout preference, settings picker, ArticlePane with empty state, list row scroll-into-view, docs (frontend-design.md sections 3 and 4).
Same URL state (?article=) in both modes; exactly one of drawer/pane mounts the state hook.
Upstream declined a 3-pane view (0x2E/fusion#158), so this stays in the fork, kept in new files where possible.

Decisions 2026-10-09:
- readingLayout is per device (localStorage), never synced to the server.
- Picker only in the settings dialog (MVP).
- Panes at every desktop width; mobile always uses the drawer.
- Default stays "drawer"; list column 400px; empty pane = lucide BookOpen + "Select an article to read".
